questions.q: The cat licked ___ paws clean.
questions.why: 'Its' is the possessive form; 'it's' means 'it is' or 'it has'.

questions.q: ___ going to rain this afternoon.
questions.why: 'It's' is the contraction of 'it is', which fits here.

questions.q: They left ___ coats in the hallway.
questions.why: 'Their' shows possession; 'there' is a place and 'they're' means 'they are'.

questions.q: Look over ___ by the window.
questions.why: 'There' refers to a place or location.

questions.q: ___ coming to the party tonight.
Is this ___ jacket on the chair?
___ going to love this movie.
We are going ___ the beach tomorrow.
questions.why: 'To' is a preposition; 'too' means 'also/excessively' and 'two' is the number.

questions.q: I would like to come ___.
She bought ___ tickets for the show.
This book is more interesting ___ that one.
questions.why: 'Than' is used for comparisons; 'then' refers to time or sequence.

questions.q: We had dinner and ___ watched a film.
questions.why: 'Then' refers to time or what happens next.

questions.q: The new policy will ___ everyone in the office.
questions.why: 'Affect' is usually a verb meaning to influence; 'effect' is usually a noun.

questions.q: The medicine had a strong ___ on him.
questions.why: 'Effect' is a noun meaning a result.

questions.q: Be careful not to ___ your keys again.
questions.why: 'Lose' is a verb meaning to misplace; 'loose' means not tight.

questions.q: These jeans feel a bit ___ on me.
questions.why: 'Loose' is an adjective meaning not tight.

questions.q: There are ___ chairs than we need.
You should drink ___ coffee.
___ knocking at the door?
___ umbrella is this?
Can you give me some ___ about my resume?
questions.why: 'Advice' is a noun; 'advise' is the verb.

questions.q: I strongly ___ you to see a doctor.
questions.why: 'Advise' is the verb meaning to give advice.

questions.q: The company increased ___ profits this year.
I think ___ right about the answer.
Type the answer: 'The team celebrated ___ victory.' (possessive of it)
Type the answer: '___ the best player on the team.' (he is)
Type the answer: 'I have ___ many things to do today.' (also/excessively)
Type the answer: 'She is taller ___ her brother.' (comparison)
Type the answer: 'Did the weather ___ your travel plans?' (verb: influence)
questions.why: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to influence.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I bought ___ books than last month.' (countable, opposite of more)
The medicine had no ___ on him at all.
questions.why: 'Effect' is the noun; 'affect' is the verb.

questions.q: These trousers are too ___ — I need a belt.
I'd rather have tea ___ coffee.
___ turn is it to cook tonight?
Everyone accepted the decision ___ the coach.
